title: iLang Protocol Specification
description:
iLang is an AI-native communication protocol that defines a formal vocabulary of 88 verbs, 29 core modifiers plus a 20-key media profile, 25 entities (17 addressable, 8 role), and 13 Greek aliases for structured communication between humans and AI, between AI agents, and within AI internal reasoning.

It introduces two syntaxes: operation syntax [] for executable instructions and declaration syntax :: for behavioral identity. Version 3.0 defines the communication format, version 4.0 adds execution semantics, and version 5.0 adds a trainable judgment layer built on an 11-dimensional judgment vector space governed by four axioms and a three-layer architecture, grounded in fuzzy mathematics.

iLang provides the semantic and judgment layer that sits above tool-integration protocols such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-discovery protocols such as Google's Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A). MIT licensed.

Release 4.2.0 extends the v4 stable line with SPEC-v4.2-MEDIA-REGIONS-AND-LAYERS.md: media regions as document-scoped entities declared with ::STATE and four body keys (pts, bnd, vtx, msk), masks by reference or by geometry, and image layers composed by MERGE with ::LIST line order as stacking order. It adds no verb, core modifier, profile key, registered entity or declaration type; the four amendments to released text are set out in its section 4.12. The grammar validator gains media gating for image layers and warning-level region body checks, and its canon gate lints the new file. The 4.1.1 validator fix (quoted values read as opaque) is carried forward.

This snapshot also carries the v5.0 preview erratum released as 5.0-pre.2.1.1: the section 4 abstain rule of SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md now also accepts M8 on a STEP-1 survival hit, following the section 3 conflict total order SURVIVAL > EPISTEMIC. The reference function, its constants and its weights are unchanged.

The media profile was first published on 2026-09-12 in release v5.0-pre.2.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22728994) and re-released on the v4 line as 4.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22729246).

Release 4.3.0 (2026-09-26) rewrote 26 statements of SPEC-v4.0-FINAL.md and SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md that asked a model to take an identity, claim an authority or set its own rules aside, so that the model perceives and code executes the decision, and added the rule that the runtime's ::BUDGET line is read and never re-emitted; SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md became 2.2.0. The A/B behind it is published at research.ilang.ai/datasets/canon-rewrite-ab.

Release 4.4.0 (2026-09-26) carries SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md 2.3.0: the document names the source it answers to, MODULE::SOURCE (whoever makes a rule is bound by it first), placed outside the axioms and unweighted by them; the Axiom 4 proposer constraints use the SELF_CHECK:E test, carry a consequence (aut below 0.30, M6) and are scoped to unconsented harm; calibration weights initialize at epsilon above 0, never at 0, and the f_v5 constants are not recalibrated; AMENDMENT gains RULE:counterexample and a non-normative Appendix F; MODULE::TRAGIC_CHOICE makes the Axiom 2 tragic branch executable (code ranks, the principal decides), with tragic_rank() in the judge validator; GENE correction gains principal_rule_error. The Part II frozen set is unchanged.

Release 4.4.1 (2026-09-26) is an erratum to 2.3.0 (SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md 2.3.1) from the same day's review: a Part I condition acts only by setting a dimension value and f_v5 decides, so the Axiom 4 consequences are written as values (aut set to 0.29, STEP-3 M6, for a proposer who exempts himself; ext set to 0.09, STEP-1 M8, for a proposer who benefits while another party bears unconsented harm), and MODULE::TRAGIC_CHOICE assigns no mode to the option set: each option keeps its f_v5 mode and the ranking is recorded and handed to the principal. The Part II frozen set is unchanged.

Release 4.5.0 (2026-09-26) carries SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md 2.4.0, in which every symbol of the normative text is defined, bound to an f_v5 constant, or registered: MODULE::ROUTING (a Part I condition acts only by setting a dimension of the vector, a value below a gate is the gate minus 0.01, and one routing table lists every stop, ask and hand-over); MODULE::MEASUREMENT (where no standard exists the quantity is a weighted combination of registered functions and constants, written out, recorded and recomputed when a better ruler appears); Axiom 1 stated as properties with the Beta model WEIGHT-BETA-1 registered (linear growth, no time decay); Axiom 2 threshold 0.20; Axiom 3 consistency read as ine with a three-sigma control chart; Axiom 4 B_ext explanatory; Layer C acting through rel with TRUST-WILSON-1; derived features explicit; U equal to S; the four boundaries derived from MODULE::SOURCE; calibration speeds as hypotheses; Appendix F counterexamples CX-002 to CX-004; Appendix G model registry. The judge validator gains the registered models and the routing table as functions with selftests. The Part II frozen set is unchanged.

Release 4.5.1 (2026-09-26) carries SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md 2.4.1, erratum CX-005 found by the first run of the new symbol audit (symbol_audit.py, now part of CI): the model-estimated quantities that Axiom 2 and Axiom 4 use are defined (budget, irreversible, consent, scope) and unconsented_harm is restated on worst_case, so that the undefined ΔU_p is gone. With it every symbol of the normative text is defined, bound to an f_v5 constant, registered in Appendix G, marked explanatory, or whitelisted with a stated reason. The Part II frozen set is unchanged.
